title: An unconfigured blend path can cause unrelated imports to fail in headless mode.
body:
### Tested versions

Found in Godot Engine v4.7.stable.official.5b4e0cb0f running in headless mode.



### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS - Azure Hosted Compute Agent

### Issue description

Running `Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64 project.godot --headless --import` on a project that contains a `.blend` file, but does not have a valid blender path set, causes unrelated imports (e.g. svg and png files) to fail. _Removing the blend file from the project fixes the issue._

We ran into this issue while setting up a CI workflow on github.

The failing imports are reported as follows and start only after the blender error.
```
ERROR: Blender path is invalid or not set, check your Editor Settings. Cannot configure blender path in headless mode.
   at: query (modules/gltf/editor/editor_scene_importer_blend.cpp:552)
ERROR: Unable to open file: res://.godot/imported/microchip.svg-cfe91c6cb2b888dacc999f44830969a2.ctex.
   at: _load_data (scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp:45)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://.godot/imported/microchip.svg-cfe91c6cb2b888dacc999f44830969a2.ctex.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:317)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://addons/fsm/microchip.svg.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:317)
ERROR: Unable to open file: res://.godot/imported/microchip.svg-cfe91c6cb2b888dacc999f44830969a2.ctex.
   at: _load_data (scene/resources/compressed_texture.cpp:45)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://.godot/imported/microchip.svg-cfe91c6cb2b888dacc999f44830969a2.ctex.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:317)
ERROR: Failed loading resource: res://addons/fsm/microchip.svg.
   at: _load (core/io/resource_loader.cpp:317)
```


### Steps to reproduce

- create a new project
- In editor settings, set the blender path to something invalid.
- add a `.blend` file to the project (running `touch a.blend` works)
- add the _signal state machine_ add-on by clearleaf.
- close the editor
- navigate to the project folder
- delete the `.godot` folder
- run `Godot_v4.7-stable_linux.x86_64 project.godot --headless --import`

If you delete the `.blend` file and run the command again, the issue should disappear. I've only been able to reproduce this issue with that specific add-on installed. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Github does not allow me to upload the MRP or a `.blend` file.
